format: Illustrated explainer, not a screen recording

scenes.title: Better coordination. More livable cities.
scenes.body: Cleaner streets. Safer roads. Healthier neighbourhoods. Help municipal teams understand civic problems and coordinate a better response.
scenes.explain: An AI agent platform connecting reports, evidence and departments—from investigation to follow-up.
scenes.caption: A broader city vision; this demo explores waterlogging, road damage and waste.
scenes.label: CIVIC PROBLEMS · CONNECTED RESPONSES

scenes.title: Connect the report to its history.
scenes.body: At Market Junction, potholes returned after earlier repairs. The road, utility records and repair history become one connected case file.
scenes.explain: Named relationships connect reports, assets and past work. A connection guides a check; it does not prove a cause.
scenes.caption: A pipe being nearby is not enough: investigate sourced connections.
scenes.label: FALKORDB DOMAIN GRAPH

scenes.title: Ask a question. Follow the evidence.
scenes.body: Could a pipe leak or weak ground explain the damage? Civicly’s AI chooses tools through MCP and compares what the records support.
scenes.explain: Graph paths retrieve related evidence. GraphRAG retrieves cited procedures from a separate document graph.
scenes.caption: Inspection evidence is attributed, dated and reviewed; alternatives remain visible.
scenes.label: AI + MCP + GRAPH RETRIEVAL

scenes.title: Turn findings into a reviewed plan.
scenes.body: Supported findings guide a response: isolate the pipe, repair the leak, verify that repair, then repair the road foundation.
scenes.explain: Departments, task dependencies and source citations support the plan. Application services enforce human approval and safety gates.
scenes.caption: Approval is for the exact plan and scope. AI advice alone cannot authorize work.
scenes.label: CONNECTED TASKS + HUMAN AUTHORITY

scenes.title: Coordinate work in the right order.
scenes.body: Water Utilities and Roads have different jobs. Road repair waits until the required utility work and verification are recorded.
scenes.explain: Approved tasks link to work orders, responsible teams and status history. Validated services enforce each transition.
scenes.caption: The demonstration uses authenticated, simulated department workflows.
scenes.label: DEPARTMENTS + DEPENDENCIES

scenes.title: Completed work is not the finish line.
scenes.body: A finished repair does not prove the problem is solved. Separate follow-up checks the declared success criteria before closure.
scenes.explain: Dated observations link the intervention to a reviewed outcome. Missing evidence keeps the case under monitoring.
scenes.caption: The road demo has recorded follow-up; it does not prove long-term durability.
scenes.label: MONITORING + OUTCOME EVIDENCE

scenes.title: Remember what happened.
scenes.body: The next investigation should know what was tried, what failed and what later evidence showed. A saved workflow can pause and resume.
scenes.explain: Case graph: evidence and outcomes. GraphRAG: sourced procedures. FalkorDBSaver: investigation checkpoints.
scenes.caption: Retained history gives a later investigation context without erasing earlier findings.
scenes.label: CASE MEMORY + KNOWLEDGE + CHECKPOINTS

scenes.title: Understand. Coordinate. Verify.
scenes.body: Connect the clues behind recurring civic problems. Help the right stakeholders address the cause—and check what happened afterwards.
scenes.explain: Connected evidence informs the agent. People approve action. Follow-up determines whether closure is justified.
scenes.caption: Explore the saved investigation: Report → Evidence → Response → Outcome.
scenes.label: CIVICLY · FROM REPORT TO RESOLUTION
